content:
When generating the HTML documentation, identifier names are resolved with respect to the scope and links are created to the definition of the identifier.
This usually works correctly, but sometimes it works incorrectly, for example on https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Tactic/CongrExclamation.html , the documentation of the congr! tactic, all mentions of congr tactic links to the congr theorem.

One way to fix this is to add the link manually, as seen in https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/44988 . What do you think about this? I feel ideally there should be a better solution, say, somehow declare that all identifiers in a file should resolve to some fully qualified name while making links, or should not resolve at all.

as snir pointed out on the PR, it would be nice not to add manual fixed which need undoing when verso docsteing are fully enabled. That means figuring out how verso docstring work exactly, which Im not super familiar with yet either. I'd assume it would allow a way to specify the fully qualified name of the tactic which get's rendered as congr to distinguish it from a declaration called congr?
@Snir Broshi already point out that prefixing {tactic} does it (somehow I overlooked this…)

I don't think we come to a conclusion on how to deal with the spacing change caused by switching to Verso yet, so I'd wait, I suppose.
(Main discussion thread: #mathlib4 > Verso in Mathlib)
